translations.text: The time of the Day of Judgement is approaching, mighty and thunderous. Trembling has seized the ridged world, throughout the rugged [?] earth.
Truth, the foundation of the ages, will be drowned. Wretched is the slaughter [?]. Every good thing will wither. Great is the wave of tribulation; woe to the one it reaches!
Evil will prevail; great will be the evil in every person. Every law will override another throughout the yellow world.
Breast and nourishment will be drowned [?]. Fierce [?] is the rout of the brood [?]. There will be no change in the reckoning for the seed of Adam.
There will be no reverence, there will be no game, there will be no assembly. Alas! A tearful time will come under holy heaven.
There will be no justice, nor law, nor rule, without [?] death. There will be no kings, and there will be no sages in their proper place.
There will be no piety in the churches, loftier than [?] treasures. There will be no valour in the young men, though they are in their hundreds.
The prophecy of the elders will come about: there will be afflictions [?], dogs, [?], war-bands, many grey ones [?]. What could be worse?
Everyone harming his neighbour, lasting strife, spears all around without blessing, cold hearts.
Many heads, little honour, [?] every [?], guilty [?] without ploughing, many diseases.
A deceitful, lying world, a heathen time, churches enslaved, many satirists, crooked weathers, perverse peoples.
Crooked judgements, lawsuits without justice against the midst of [?], every [?] after the loss of his honour, a sorrowful time.
Trembling upon the elements, a shore without produce, a people without wisdom, acceptance [?] of crimes, a time of vengeance, many languages.
An age without learning, everyone in great [?], the order weary, justice without firmness; every law will turn away from its rule.
Every woman a serpent, every girl a griffin, bitter their ways, full greens [?], much gluttony, empty storehouses.
Woods without blossoms, everyone in outlawry, an abundance of [?], a half-green time, sons with [?], land with re-measuring [?].
Everyone in despair forever, long-lasting vengeance, small people, garments of death [?], many wars.
Fierce giants [?], heavy [?], a causeway of anger, frequent raids, an abundance of rage [?], red graveyards.
What shall we do about it, O Son of God, against the customary [?]? The [?] of Judgement have arisen; our peoples cry out [?].
Treasures [?] have come into the world; it would have been better to [?] them. Alas! [?] in the course of the road [?].
A son will come into the world [?], a strong, cunning man; his own sister will be his mother.
A girl will lie with her father like a serpent; of her [?] will be the son who will be born in the city.
His teeth a single plate, [?] my tidings, [?] after walls; six toes on his slender feet, in the mysteries [?].
A bitter, withered [?] man, a scourger of hell (true is my statement), a dark, swift judge, and a grey tuft out of his forehead.
He will make gold out of the soft [?] clods of the plain. What is more desirable?
